end_to_end.expected: Each review lists exactly the opponents in record.shown (user's seat left out), in record order, with their cards. These match the table's shown and winner cards. No card outside user cards, board and shown cards appears in the panel's text, innerText/textContent, any attribute value, <title> text, aria snapshot or data-card. Fold-outs and hands where only the user shows have no list. Only same-origin requests.

Every row matched the record and the table. 0 hidden-card traces across 39 to 46 hidden cards per hand. Panel has no horizontal overflow. Only same-origin requests. Both browsers pass.

items.evidence: The acceptance test passes. It asserts one list placed directly after .review-head's and before Decisions, one li with data-review-shown=2, text 'Ben showed · Pair of kings', group 'Ben's shown cards' with Kd, 7c and labels King of diamonds / Seven of clubs, for REVIEW_DEE_MUCKS and REVIEW_LOST_48. Holdout: in 468 random-session reviews, every row's text starts with ' showed' and its cards equal record.shown.

The acceptance test passes. It first asserts that Dee was really dealt 5c 5d and the folders their cards (not vacuous). It then searches text, aria-label/title/alt, <title>, whole-word codes and glyphs, bans 'Pair of fives', and uses an exact data-card allow-list. Holdout: 1,796 mucked or folded opponent hands searched in rendered TableView panels (all attributes, names, glyphs, codes, data-card): 0 traces. A detector sanity check confirms a rendered card is flagged.

The acceptance test passes: RAISE_TAKES_BLINDS has no list, data-card exactly [Ah, 9s], and none of the 5 opponents' cards appear. Holdout: 103 fold-out reviews in random sessions, all with no list and no hidden card; the live app fold-outs also have no list.

The acceptance test passes: a deep walk of summary/shown/entries for 4 fixtures, no deck/players/burned keys, every holeCards/board value in user ∪ board ∪ record.shown, and the rendered ReviewPanel passes the search for non-shown opponent seats. The recorded deviation (user seat left out of the search because the header always shows the user's own cards) is correct in substance. Holdout: in random sessions every panel data-card is in user ∪ board ∪ record.shown.

The acceptance test passes: shownOpponents equals record.shown minus the user. The variant Qh Qs (cards never dealt to Dee) renders Qh Qs with no 5c/5d/Kd/7c, which proves the cards come from shown data and not from a re-deal. shown:null gives no list. The source ban on shuffledDeck/createHand/dealHand holds in the 3 files (re-checked in the diff).

Both unit tests pass with exact values for the 5 fixtures, the mutation-isolation check and RangeError('Seat 9 is not at the table'). Holdout boundaries: only-user-shown gives [] and no list; empty shown gives []; showdown order is kept (seat 6 before seat 1, not sorted); returned holeCards is a fresh array; seat 0 throws RangeError; a name with HTML is escaped; the default shown prop renders identically to shown=[].
npm run e2e: review-shown scene and fold-out tests pass in Chromium and WebKit (text, group cards, hidden-card search over every element, page-wide 5c/5d count 0, no overflow, axe, no http requests).

The pinned-words live test passes in both browsers. Holdout: 35 live reviews with random replay codes in both browsers. Rows equal record.shown minus the user and match the table's shown and winner cards. 0 traces of any of the 52 cards outside the allowed set, in attributes, text or the aria snapshot. Only same-origin requests.
